en: Itivuttaka 24:
Ekakanipāta,
Third Chapter (Tatiyavagga)
The Discourse on the Heap of Bones.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One; so I have heard:

“Monks, for a single person wandering and transmigrating for an eon, there might be such a great heap of bones, such a pile of bones, such a mass of bones as this mountain Vepulla, if there were one to collect them and that collection were not to perish.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"By one person, in one eon..."
"A heap of a person's bones might become a pile as large as a mountain," so it was said by the Great Seer.
And so this great mountain Vepulla has been described,
which lies to the north of Vulture Peak.
In Giribbaja, among the Magadhans.
But when one perceives the Noble Truths with right wisdom;
Suffering, the origin of suffering,
and the transcendence of suffering;
and the Noble Eightfold Path—
Leading to the stilling of suffering—
that person, having wandered through rebirth at most seven times;
“He becomes one who makes an end of suffering through the destruction of all fetters.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth.
